items.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
items.why: Google's new frontier model is out: #1 on the Vals Index, 1M-token context, strong at agentic coding and document analysis, API at $2 per million input tokens with 50% off through November. The new bar Claude gets measured against.

items.title: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
items.why: An open-weight 24B model with only 2B active parameters, built for tool calling inside agent harnesses and supported by llama.cpp and vLLM from day one. A cheap local-agent candidate, though a 12 GB GPU will need quantization or offload.

items.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
items.why: Any shopper's AI agent can now browse and buy from over a billion Shopify listings, with budget rules and a human approving every purchase. A real-world template for letting agents act while a person signs off.

items.title: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
items.why: An explainer, not news: it starts from Anthropic's warning that the open GLM-5.3 model can aid cyberattacks and weighs open-weight benefits against risks. Useful context on where rules for local models may head.

items.title: Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
items.why: The Play Store will let people privately host and share apps they built with AI, alongside new AI search for apps. Could become an easy home for personal tools that never need a public release.

items.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
items.why: A court ordered OpenAI to hand over hiring records in Apple's trade-secrets case, a sign the AI talent war is moving into court. Ranked from the headline only.

items.title: Disney offers $20M for Character.AI’s scandal-plagued chatbot tech
items.why: Disney's $20M offer for Character.AI's chatbot tech shows how far companion-chatbot startups have fallen after their safety scandals. Ranked from the headline only.

items.title: Facebook will let you customize your feed algorithm using AI
items.why: Facebook users will be able to steer their feed by telling an AI what they want, a first large test of plain-language control over a recommendation algorithm. Ranked from the headlines only.

items.title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
items.why: Xbox is backing AI-powered ports of older games, an example of AI doing large-scale work on legacy code. Ranked from the headline only.

items.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
items.why: A $42M round for a startup tackling the security problems AI creates inside companies, a steady signal that AI governance is becoming its own product category. Ranked from the headline only.
